en: "Venerable Nāgasena, as for this which you call 'saṃsāra' (the wandering-on), what is that saṃsāra?

"Here, Great King, one is born and dies right here; having died here, one arises elsewhere. Having been born there, one dies right there; having died there, one arises elsewhere. It is in this way, Great King, that saṃsāra exists."
“Suppose, great king, a certain man, having eaten a ripe mango, were to plant its stone;
from that a great mango tree would grow and yield fruit, and then that same man, having again eaten a ripe mango from it...”
“Suppose one were to plant a seed, and from it a great mango tree were to arise and bear fruit;
even so, the end of these trees cannot be discerned.

In the same way, Great King, one born here dies right here; having died here, one arises elsewhere. Born there, one dies right there; having died there, one arises elsewhere. Such, Great King, is the nature of saṃsāra.”
Thus ends the ninth chapter, the Chapter on Saṃsāra.
